title: Al-'Adiyat 100:5-8 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: Al-'Adiyat, Az-Zalzalah and reading from the mushaf
source: Written for quran/y2 lesson 49 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-'Adiyat 100:5-8 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 49. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِۦ جَمْعًا (٥) إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لِرَبِّهِۦ لَكَنُودٌۭ (٦) وَإِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌۭ (٧) وَإِنَّهُۥ لِحُبِّ ٱلْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ (٨)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Arriving thereby in the center collectively,
Indeed mankind, to his Lord, is ungrateful.
And indeed, he is to that a witness.
And indeed he is, in love of wealth, intense.

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-'Adiyat 100:5-8 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 100:5-8 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Say 'alhamdulillah' for three things at dinner tonight.
questions.a: For example: food, water, my family.
A) ungrateful to their Lord. 100:6: 'Indeed mankind, to his Lord, is ungrateful.'

questions.q: Al-'Adiyat 100:6: «إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Allah gives us so much. Why do people sometimes forget to say thank you?
questions.a: They love things too much and forget the Giver; Al-'Adiyat says people are ungrateful to their Lord (100:6).
